title: Marked mapping-simplex presentations determine coherent transport
statement:
Use [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration], and the straightening equivalence $\operatorname{St}_S:\operatorname{coCart}(S)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(S,\mathrm{Cat}_\infty)$ of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. Work in a common containing universe. Let $C$ be a small ordinary category and $D:C\to\mathsf{sSet}$ a strict functor with quasicategory values. Define $R_C(D)$ by the following simplices: an $n$-simplex consists of $\sigma:[n]\to C$ and maps $t_J:\Delta^J\to D(\sigma(\max J))$ for every nonempty $J\subseteq[n]$, with
$$t_J|_{\Delta^I}=D(\sigma(\max I)\to\sigma(\max J))t_I\quad(\varnothing\ne I\subseteq J).$$
An operator $\theta:[m]\to[n]$ sends these data to $\sigma\theta$ and $t'_J=t_{\theta(J)}\circ\Delta(\theta|_J)$. Projection to $\sigma$ defines $r:R_C(D)\to N(C)$. There is a simplicial map $i_D:G_C(D)\to R_C(D)$ over $N(C)$ given on $(\sigma,\tau)$ by $t_J=D(\sigma(0)\to\sigma(\max J))(\tau|_{\Delta^J})$.

Then $r$ is a cocartesian fibration classified by the coherent diagram $D$, with fibres $D(c)$. An edge over $f:c\to d$ is $r$-cocartesian precisely when its edge in $D(d)$ is an equivalence. For every cocartesian fibration $q:Q\to N(C)$, precomposition with $i_D$ is an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{cocart}}_{/N(C)}(R_C(D),Q)\xrightarrow{\simeq}\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{mark}}_{/N(C)}(G_C(D),Q).$$
Each side is the full subcategory of the simplicial mapping object over $N(C)$ on maps preserving the indicated edges: all cocartesian edges on the left and the marked edges of $G_C(D)$ on the right; its higher simplices are arbitrary transformations over the base. The comparison is compatible with postcomposition by cocartesian maps, with strict transformations of $D$, and with pullback along $N(u)$ for functors $u:C'\to C$.

Consequently a strict presentation $\varphi:G_C(D)\to Q$ determines an equivalence $\alpha_\varphi:D\simeq\operatorname{St}_{N(C)}(q)$ whose component at $c$ is the fibre equivalence $\varphi_c:D(c)\to Q_c$ and whose transport edges are $\varphi(f,s_0x)$. This identification is coherent over all simplices. For another strict presentation $\varphi'$ of $q':Q'\to N(C)$, a strict transformation $\eta:D\to D'$ and a cocartesian map $g:Q\to Q'$ with $g\varphi=\varphi'G_C(\eta)$, there is a coherent natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{St}(g)\alpha_\varphi\simeq\alpha_{\varphi'}\eta.$$
These identifications commute coherently with pullback in $C$.

source.place: Definition 3.2.5.2, Remarks 3.2.5.4 and 3.2.5.7, and Proposition 3.2.5.21 for the relative nerve. The marked mapping-simplex comparison is the global form of Proposition 3.2.2.14 (cocartesian dual), with the relative-nerve comparison of §3.2.5. Kerodon Proposition 5.6.4.8 (Subsection tag 0279) compares the weighted nerve with the category of elements; Definition 5.6.5.1 (028V) defines transport representation. The general marked mapping-object and naturality formulation is an agent-formulated foundation, not quoted verbatim as a proposition in HTT. Read online; WANTED: archived HTT and Kerodon. No matching Stacks tag.

proof.text: Set $S=N(C)$ and choose one universe containing $C,Q$ and all fibres and mapping objects to be used, with a larger universe for their collections. The operators defining $R_C(D)$ preserve its equations: for $I\subseteq J$, restriction of $t_{\theta(J)}\Delta(\theta|_J)$ to $\Delta^I$ equals $D(\sigma(\max\theta(I))\to\sigma(\max\theta(J)))t_{\theta(I)}\Delta(\theta|_I)$. Composition of two operators is composition of their monotone maps. For $i_D$, restriction to $I\subseteq J$ satisfies the required equation by $D(\sigma(0)\to\sigma(\max J))=D(\sigma(\max I)\to\sigma(\max J))D(\sigma(0)\to\sigma(\max I))$. To compare $i_D$ with an operator $\theta$, the formula for $G_C(D)$ in [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration] first applies $D(\sigma(0)\to\sigma(\theta(0)))$ to $\theta^*\tau$; the remaining map to $D(\sigma(\theta(\max J)))$ composes to the same $D(\sigma(0)\to\sigma(\theta(\max J)))$. Thus $i_D$ is simplicial. The fibre over $c$ is $D(c)$: on a constant string the equations say $t_J=t_{[n]}|_{\Delta^J}$. The fibre map of $i_D$ is the identity.

source.place: Definition 3.2.5.2 and Remarks 3.2.5.4/7: explicit operators and comparison formula; compare the mapping-simplex formula of §3.2.2, dualized.

proof.text: Give each $D(c)$ the marking of its equivalences, writing $F(c)=D(c)^\natural$. A simplicial map preserves inverse edges and their two triangle witnesses, so the maps $D(f)$ preserve this marking. By [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], these are fibrant objects of the absolute marked model, so $F$ is projectively fibrant. Apply [lem-cbc-marked-relative-nerve-quillen]. Its explicit relative nerve is exactly $R_C(D)$, and its edge marking is exactly that an edge $t_{\{0,1\}}$ in the last fibre is an equivalence. The right Quillen property and [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model] make $r$ a cocartesian fibration and identify this marking with all its cocartesian edges. The derived comparison with unstraightening, followed by [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], gives a coherent equivalence $\kappa_D:D\simeq\operatorname{St}_S(r)$, with coherently identified identity fibre maps and the transport $D(f)$. For a marked edge $(f,s_0x)$ of $G_C(D)$, its image has $t_{\{0,1\}}=s_0D(f)x$, so is cocartesian. This also verifies that $i_D$ is a marked map.

source.place: Definition 3.2.5.12, Proposition 3.2.5.18(2), Corollary 3.2.5.20; derive the cocartesian-fibration and marking clauses of Proposition 3.2.5.21.

proof.text: Fix any simplex $\sigma:\Delta^n\to N(C)$, corresponding to a functor $[n]\to C$. Degreewise pullback identifies $G_C(D)\times_S\Delta^n$ with $G_{[n]}(D\sigma)$: an $m$-simplex is a monotone $\rho:[m]\to[n]$ and $\tau\in D(\sigma(\rho(0)))_m$, with the operators and marking of [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration]. The pullback $r_\sigma$ is a cocartesian fibration by [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model]. The map $(i_D)_\sigma$ preserves marked edges by step 2 and is the identity on all vertex fibres by step 1. To apply the existing Cartesian mapping-simplex theorem [lem-coef-cartesian-mapping-simplex-presentation], take opposites and identify $(\Delta^n)^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $\Delta^n$ by vertex reversal. Put $A_j=D(\sigma(j))$ and $B_j=A_{n-j}^{\mathrm{op}}$. The transitions form $B_0\leftarrow\cdots\leftarrow B_n$. More explicitly, an $m$-simplex of the reversed source over $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ corresponds to $\rho(j)=n-\alpha(m-j)$ and $\tau\in(A_{n-\alpha(m)})_m$, hence to $a\in(B_{\alpha(m)})_m$. For $\theta:[k]\to[m]$, the operator on the unreversed source is $\theta^{\mathrm{rev}}(l)=m-\theta(k-l)$. Its first vertex is $\rho(\theta^{\mathrm{rev}}(0))=n-\alpha(\theta(k))$. Thus the operator on $a$ first restricts by $\theta$ in the opposite simplicial set and then applies the chain map $B_{\alpha(m)}\to B_{\alpha\theta(k)}$. This is exactly the last-vertex operator in the cited mapping-simplex statement. Reversal takes a degenerate fibre edge to a degenerate fibre edge, so the markings also agree. Thus the opposite of $(i_D)_\sigma$ is a marked map from its $M^m(B)$ into the Cartesian fibration $r_\sigma^{\mathrm{op}}$, with identity fibre maps. The theorem makes it a Cartesian equivalence. Taking opposites back, as in the relative-model theorem, makes $(i_D)_\sigma$ a relative cocartesian weak equivalence. Degenerate base simplices are included, and no injectivity or fibrancy of $G$ is assumed.

source.place: Definition 3.2.2.6 and Proposition 3.2.2.14, cocartesian dual obtained by taking opposite fibres and reversing the simplex vertices.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-marked-mapping-simplex-descent] to the marked map $i_D$ over the small quasicategory $S=N(C)$, using step 3 for every simplex. It gives, for every $q:Q\to S$, an equivalence of the full marked mapping quasicategories from $R_C(D)$ and $G_C(D)$ into $Q$. With the marking of step 2 on $R_C(D)$ these are precisely $\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{cocart}}_{/S}(R_C(D),Q)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{mark}}_{/S}(G_C(D),Q)$ in the statement. The degree-$k$ map is $H\mapsto H\circ(i_D\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^k})$. Thus it is the claimed precomposition comparison on all transformations and higher simplices. No inference from an equivalence on cores alone is being made.

source.place: Marked relative-model skeletal descent, using the criterion of Proposition 3.1.3.3 and the gluing mechanism of Proposition 3.2.2.8.

proof.text: For a strict presentation $\varphi$, essential surjectivity of step 4 supplies a cocartesian map $h:R_C(D)\to Q$ together with a coherent natural equivalence $\epsilon:h i_D\simeq\varphi$ over $S$. Restricting to $c$ and using $(i_D)_c=\mathrm{id}$ gives $h_c\simeq\varphi_c$, so $h_c$ is an equivalence. The fibre criterion in [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model] makes $h$ an equivalence in $\operatorname{coCart}(S)$. Define $\alpha_\varphi=\operatorname{St}(h)\kappa_D$ using [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. It is an equivalence. The fibre identification is $\varphi_c$ via $\epsilon_c$. Evaluating the entire transformation $\epsilon$ on a marked edge $(f,s_0x)$ gives the comparison of $h(i_D(f,s_0x))$ with $\varphi(f,s_0x)$, with the fibre identifications inserted. On every higher simplex its restriction is the corresponding higher naturality datum, because $\epsilon$ is a simplexwise transformation over $S$, not a list of unrelated edge homotopies. This realizes the prescribed components and transport edges with all their coherence.

source.place: Corollary 3.2.5.20 and Proposition 3.2.5.21(3), together with the fibrewise equivalence criterion for marked fibrations (§3.1.3).

proof.text: Let $\eta:D\to D'$ be strict. Define $R(\eta)$ on a relative-nerve simplex by $t_J\mapsto\eta_{\sigma(\max J)}t_J$. Naturality of $\eta$ verifies its compatibility equations and gives the strict identity $R(\eta)i_D=i_{D'}G(\eta)$; this identity uses the displayed formula for $i_D$ on each $J$, not just its action on vertices. $R(\eta)$ preserves cocartesian edges because a functor of the fibre quasicategories preserves equivalences. Postcomposition by any cocartesian $g:Q\to Q'$ commutes with the map in step 4 in every parameter degree: $gH(i_D\times1)=(gH)(i_D\times1)$. Similarly, precomposition by $R(\eta)$ and $G(\eta)$ gives a commuting square of the same restriction functors. These equalities commute with every monotone operator on $\Delta^k$. Together with the diagram naturality in [lem-cbc-marked-relative-nerve-quillen], they prove the stated postcomposition and strict-transformation compatibility of the mapping comparison.

source.place: Remarks 3.2.5.4/14/16: explicit naturality of the relative nerve and the comparison with unstraightening.

proof.text:
Choose extensions $(h,\epsilon)$ and $(h',\epsilon')$ for $\varphi$ and $\varphi'$. Under the hypothesis $g\varphi=\varphi'G(\eta)$, the restrictions of $g h$ and $h'R(\eta)$ along $i_D$ are coherently equivalent: use $g\epsilon$, this strict hypothesis, and the inverse of $\epsilon'G(\eta)$ in that order. The mapping-space clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] applied to the equivalence in step 4 with target $Q'$ gives equivalences of Kan mapping spaces; in particular it lifts the displayed comparison to a transformation $\lambda:g h\to h'R(\eta)$ together with its specified restriction equivalence. Lift the inverse comparison by the same mapping-space equivalence. The two inverse equations lift as well, because the induced maps on those mapping spaces are equivalences. These witnesses make $\lambda$ a coherent natural equivalence $g h\simeq h'R(\eta)$. The space of such lifts with its specified restriction equivalence is contractible: it is the homotopy fibre over that equivalence of an equivalence of Kan mapping spaces, hence contractible by [lem-coef-space-contractible-fiber-equivalence]. Hence the lift retains all higher compatibility data. Apply the functor [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] and the naturality $\operatorname{St}(R(\eta))\kappa_D\simeq\kappa_{D'}\eta$ from [lem-cbc-marked-relative-nerve-quillen]. Substitution gives
$$\operatorname{St}(g)\alpha_\varphi=\operatorname{St}(gh)\kappa_D\simeq\operatorname{St}(h')\operatorname{St}(R(\eta))\kappa_D\simeq\alpha_{\varphi'}\eta.$$
This is the requested natural equivalence; it compares exactly the given presentations because its restriction was built from $g\epsilon$, the specified equality, and $\epsilon'$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.3 and Corollary 3.2.5.20: mapping-space full faithfulness and naturality of the classifying comparison.

proof.text: Finally let $u:C'\to C$. On both sides of $R_{C'}(Du)=N(u)^*R_C(D)$, an $n$-simplex is $\sigma:[n]\to C'$ and the same family $t_J$ valued in $D(u\sigma(\max J))$. The operators and marked-edge tests agree. The identical check using the first vertex gives $G_{C'}(Du)=N(u)^*G_C(D)$ by [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration], and the formula for $i_D$ becomes the formula for $i_{Du}$. A strict presentation pulls back to one because its vertex maps remain $\varphi_{u(c')}$ and pullback preserves cocartesian edges [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model]. Pull back $h$ and $\epsilon$; they are an extension and equivalence for this pulled-back presentation. The base-change clauses of [lem-cbc-marked-relative-nerve-quillen] and [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] identify the resulting $\alpha$ with $\alpha_\varphi N(u)$. For the choices themselves, restrict the equivalence of step 4 to maximal Kan cores. Its quasi-inverse and its inverse-triangle transformations restrict to these cores, so the induced map is an equivalence of Kan spaces. The space of pairs $(h,\epsilon)$ extending a specified presentation is its homotopy fibre over that presentation, hence is contractible by [lem-coef-space-contractible-fiber-equivalence]. In particular a previously chosen extension of the pulled-back presentation is equivalent to the pulled-back pair, including the specified equivalence to the presentation. These identifications are coherent: iterated pullback reindexes each $\sigma,t_J$ by the same composite functor, and all lifted comparisons come from the equivalences of full mapping quasicategories, whose induced maps on Kan mapping spaces are equivalences by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] and whose homotopy fibres of choices are contractible by [lem-coef-space-contractible-fiber-equivalence]. Thus identities, composites and higher compatibilities agree, proving every pullback and naturality clause.

source.place: Remarks 3.2.5.7/14 and natural base change for straightening: degreewise pullback identities and their coherence.

split_report.summary: Retained the assigned statement. Gave an eight-step argument from explicit simplicial formulas, a relative-nerve Quillen theorem, the existing Cartesian mapping-simplex theorem applied to opposite fibres and reversed vertices, and marked simplex descent. Added explicit citations for full faithfulness on Kan mapping spaces and contractibility of homotopy fibres of equivalences. Two independent foundations remain statement-only; the draft duplicate local comparison node was removed. Second reading expanded the reversal operators and the inverse/triangle witnesses for the lifted comparison; it retained the statement and both new foundations.

tool_uses.why: Absolute marked fibrant objects identify the equivalence marking on each quasicategory fibre; the compact-support unit has no model-category theorem.
Relative marked model fibrancy, pullback and fibrewise detection of equivalences are generic model tools absent from this unit.
Use the existing classifying equivalence, including its action on maps and base change; the compact-support unit has no general straightening theorem.
The general local marked comparison is used on opposite fibres with reversed simplex vertices; no local compact-support unit result gives this simplicial theorem.
An equivalence of quasicategories induces equivalences of their Kan mapping spaces; this generic coherent functor theorem justifies lifting presentation comparisons.
Homotopy fibres of equivalences of Kan spaces are contractible; this generic space theorem justifies coherent uniqueness of lifts.
